verdict.rationale: Morph documents a `service_tier: "standby"` option that runs requests on spare capacity at half price and is explicitly "built for batch and background workloads", so a documented 50% discount for batch-style traffic exists. However, standby is a deprioritized per-request tier that returns a fast 429 when busy, not an asynchronous job API where you submit work and collect results later. Missing for 10: an async batch job submission API (job IDs, polling or result retrieval, bulk file input), queued completion guarantees instead of 429 shedding, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the discount.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can submit asynchronous batch inference jobs at a documented discount versus real-time pricing

citations.quote: Built for batch and background workloads where a retry costs nothing.
